Areas.Name: Big Woods
Areas.Description: Explore Laura's Wisconsin beginnings while keeping actual life, the books, television, and imagined learning adventures clearly separated.

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: In which state was Laura Ingalls Wilder born in 1867?
Questions.Hint: Her birthplace was near Pepin and Lake Pepin.
Questions.SuccessText: Laura was born near Pepin, Wisconsin, in 1867. Her family later lived in several other states.
Questions.SourceTitle: Laura Ingalls Wilder — Homestead National Historical Park

Questions.Prompt: Book: What kind of home is the main setting of Little House in the Big Woods?
Options: A sod dugout beside Plum Creek
A log house in the Wisconsin woods
A town house in De Smet
Questions.Hint: The title names both the size of the home and its surroundings.
Questions.SuccessText: The book centers on a log house in the Wisconsin woods. This is a book setting, not a summary of every place Laura lived.
Questions.SourceTitle: The Little House Series — Library of Congress NLS

Questions.Prompt: General science: Which observation best identifies an evergreen tree in winter?
Options: It grows only beside a creek
It keeps most of its green needles
Questions.Hint: The word evergreen describes a year-round pattern.
Questions.SuccessText: Most evergreens keep green needles through winter, although they still shed and replace some needles.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: Pa's surviving fiddle is displayed in a museum. What kind of historical source is the fiddle?
Questions.Hint: Historians learn from objects as well as written records.
Questions.SuccessText: A surviving object from the past is a physical artifact. Pa's fiddle helps connect family stories with material evidence.
Questions.SourceTitle: New Facilities for the Cather and Wilder Sites — National Park Service

Questions.Prompt: Imagined cabin experiment: Four warm cups cool by 2, 4, 6, and 9 degrees. The wool-wrapped cup cools by 2 degrees. Which wrap kept in the most heat?
Questions.Hint: The smallest temperature drop means the most heat stayed in the cup.
Questions.SuccessText: The wool-wrapped cup changed by only 2 degrees, so it kept in the most heat in this imagined test.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Imagined woodpile: Laura stacks 3 rows with 4 logs in each row. How many logs are in the pile?
Questions.Hint: Add 4 + 4 + 4, or multiply 3 by 4.
Questions.SuccessText: Three equal groups of four make 12 logs. This is an imagined math situation, not a documented event.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

Questions.Prompt: Book study: The Little House books draw from Laura's memories but reshape events into stories. Which label fits best?
Questions.Hint: The stories connect to a real life but were crafted as novels.
Questions.SuccessText: Autobiographical fiction uses life experience while selecting, arranging, or changing details to make a story.
Questions.SourceTitle: Pioneer Girl: The Path into Fiction

Questions.Prompt: Classic TV adaptation: Who portrayed Laura Ingalls during the original show's nine-season run?
Questions.Hint: PBS's documentary includes the actor remembering her audition for Laura.
Questions.SuccessText: Melissa Gilbert portrayed Laura Ingalls. This is a fact about the classic TV adaptation, not about Laura's actual-life appearance.
Questions.SourceTitle: Laura Ingalls Wilder: Prairie to Page — PBS American Masters

Areas.Name: Kansas Prairie
Areas.Description: Study prairie ecology, the Ingalls family's Kansas stay, and Osage sovereignty without treating the land as empty or unclaimed.

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: The Ingalls family settled in Kansas before that land was legally open to non-Native settlers. Whose reserved land was it?
Questions.Hint: Name the Native nation connected to the Kansas setting.
Questions.SuccessText: The family settled within the Osage Diminished Reserve. The land was an Osage homeland, not empty territory waiting to be claimed.
Questions.SourceTitle: It Began With Grazing — Osage Nation

Questions.Prompt: Social studies: What does it mean to recognize the Osage Nation as a sovereign Native nation?
Options: It existed only inside a novel
It is a living political community with its own government
It is another name for prairie weather
It has no connection to land or law
Questions.Hint: Native nations are present-day communities and governments, not only people of the past.
Questions.SuccessText: Sovereignty means Native nations have enduring political identity and powers of self-government.
Questions.SourceTitle: Native Knowledge 360° Essential Understandings

Questions.Prompt: Book: How does the Ingalls family travel from Wisconsin toward the Kansas prairie?
Questions.Hint: Think about transportation available to a moving settler family in the late 1860s.
Questions.SuccessText: In the book, the family travels by covered wagon. The book rearranges the chronology of Laura's real childhood.
Questions.SourceTitle: The Little House Series — Library of Congress NLS

Questions.Prompt: General science: Which description best fits a prairie ecosystem?
Options: Permanent ice with almost no plants
Salt water deeper than sunlight reaches
Bare rock above the tree line
Grass-dominated land with connected plants, animals, soil, and weather
Questions.Hint: An ecosystem includes both living and nonliving parts.
Questions.SuccessText: A prairie is more than open grass. It is an ecosystem of grasses, flowering plants, animals, soils, water, fire, and weather.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Imagined prairie camp: Two water containers hold 3 liters each. How many liters do they hold altogether?
Questions.Hint: Combine two equal groups of 3.
Questions.SuccessText: Three plus three equals 6 liters. This is an imagined measurement problem, not a claim about the Ingalls family.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

Questions.Prompt: Weather study: Which pair of observations gives the strongest evidence that a storm may be approaching?
Options: One old photograph and a map key
Falling air pressure and growing dark clouds
A fixed compass direction and dry soil
A calendar date and a store price
Questions.Hint: Choose measurements and observations that can change as a storm develops.
Questions.SuccessText: Falling air pressure and developing storm clouds are related weather evidence. One clue alone is less reliable.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Classic TV adaptation: Which actor portrayed Charles 'Pa' Ingalls?
Questions.Hint: He was both the show's star and a producer.
Questions.SuccessText: Michael Landon portrayed Charles 'Pa' Ingalls and also worked as a producer on the series.
Questions.SourceTitle: Peacock: Original Little House Cast and Series

Questions.Prompt: Source detective: What is the fairest way to compare an Osage history source, a historical record about the Ingalls family, a novel, and a TV episode?
Options: Treat the most colorful source as true
Use only the source written latest
Label each source and compare its evidence and purpose
Questions.Hint: Different sources were created by different people for different reasons.
Questions.SuccessText: Good historical inquiry identifies makers, dates, purposes, and evidence while including perspectives that settler stories often omitted.
Questions.SourceTitle: C3 Framework for Social Studies

Areas.Name: Plum Creek
Areas.Description: Investigate the Ingalls family's Minnesota home, prairie weather and farming, and the difference between documented experience and crafted story.

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: What kind of home did the Ingalls family first occupy beside Plum Creek near Walnut Grove?
Options: A sod dugout built into the creek bank
A brick apartment above a store
A stone castle on a hill
Questions.Hint: Part of the home used the earth itself for walls and shelter.
Questions.SuccessText: The family lived in a sod dugout beside Plum Creek. The remaining depression in the bank helps identify the historic site.
Questions.SourceTitle: Wilder, Laura Ingalls — Minnesota Historical Society

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: What damaged crops and helped push the Ingalls family to leave the Walnut Grove area in the 1870s?
Options: A change in the ocean tide
Questions.Hint: Large numbers of insects affected farms across the region.
Questions.SuccessText: Grasshopper infestations destroyed crops across Minnesota and caused serious financial hardship for farming families.
Questions.SourceTitle: Grasshopper Plagues, 1873–1877 — Minnesota Historical Society

Questions.Prompt: Book study: On the Banks of Plum Creek uses a real place and family experiences inside a crafted novel. What should a careful reader conclude?
Options: Every conversation must be a word-for-word record
No part can connect to real history
The book can mix documented experience with shaped storytelling
A novel and a land deed are the same kind of source
Questions.Hint: A historical setting does not turn a novel into an unchanged transcript.
Questions.SuccessText: The novel draws from life while shaping scenes, chronology, and dialogue. Historical claims still need corroboration.
Questions.SourceTitle: Pioneer Girl: The Path into Fiction

Questions.Prompt: General science: After heavy rain, moving creek water carries soil away from a bank. What process is occurring?
Questions.Hint: The process moves weathered material from one place to another.
Questions.SuccessText: Erosion happens when water, wind, ice, or gravity transports soil and rock.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Imagined kitchen task: Eight equal bread rolls are baked, and half are packed for later. How many rolls are packed?
Questions.Hint: Divide 8 into two equal groups.
Questions.SuccessText: Half of 8 is 4. This is an imagined fraction problem rather than a documented family event.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

Questions.Prompt: Imagined sod-wall test: Which plan best compares how two wall materials hold heat?
Options: Change material, wall thickness, and starting temperature
Change only the wall material and keep other conditions alike
Measure one wall but not the other
Questions.Hint: A useful comparison changes one main variable.
Questions.SuccessText: Keeping conditions alike makes wall material the tested variable, so the evidence is easier to interpret.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Questions.Prompt: Classic TV adaptation: How many original seasons make up the classic series?
Questions.Hint: The complete run was longer than five seasons but shorter than ten.
Questions.SuccessText: The classic television series ran for nine seasons. Its episodes are TV adaptation canon, separate from book and actual-life records.
Questions.SourceTitle: Peacock: Original Little House Cast and Series

Questions.Prompt: Geography: Rain falling on nearby slopes drains toward Plum Creek. What is the land area that drains to the creek called?
Questions.Hint: The term describes where surface water collects and flows to a common outlet.
Questions.SuccessText: A watershed is the land area whose water drains to a shared stream, river, lake, or other outlet.
Questions.SourceTitle: Next Generation Science Standards Topic Arrangements

Areas.Name: Schoolhouse and Learning
Areas.Description: Learn about Laura's teaching, Mary's education, reading evidence, and school skills through sourced history and labeled imagined practice.

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: About how old was Laura when she began working as a teacher?
Questions.Hint: She was still in her teens.
Questions.SuccessText: Laura began teaching at about age 15 in Dakota Territory, years before she became a published author.
Questions.SourceTitle: Laura Ingalls Wilder — Homestead National Historical Park

Questions.Prompt: Actual-life timeline: Laura was born in 1867 and began teaching at about age 15. About what year was that?
Questions.Hint: Add 15 years to 1867.
Questions.SuccessText: 1867 + 15 is 1882, so Laura began teaching at about that time.
Questions.SourceTitle: Laura Ingalls Wilder — Homestead National Historical Park

Questions.Prompt: Book: In Little Town on the Prairie, what important educational step does Mary take?
Options: She moves to the Kansas cabin
Questions.Hint: The event expands Mary's opportunity to learn away from home.
Questions.SuccessText: Mary, who is blind, leaves for college. Her education is an important part of both the book narrative and her life story.
Questions.SourceTitle: The Little House Series — Library of Congress NLS

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: Which statement best describes Mary Ingalls's education after she became blind?
Options: She stopped learning to read in any form
She was allowed to study only arithmetic
She attended college and used several tactile reading systems
Questions.Hint: Accessibility can provide more than one way to read and learn.
Questions.SuccessText: Mary attended the Iowa College for the Blind and used tactile systems including braille and raised print. Her story is one of education and skill, not helplessness.
Questions.SourceTitle: Museum to Host Birthday Party in Honor of Mary Ingalls — American Printing House for the Blind

Questions.Prompt: Reading evidence: Which source would best support the claim that Laura taught school as a teenager?
Options: A documented biography citing her life records
A guess based on her book titles
Questions.Hint: Choose a source created to document actual life.
Questions.SuccessText: A reliable, sourced biography provides relevant evidence. A costume or imagined scene does not establish the claim.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

Questions.Prompt: Imagined writing lesson: Which revision makes this sentence more precise? 'The weather was bad.'
Options: Freezing wind drove snow across the schoolyard.
Questions.Hint: Precise details help a reader picture the conditions.
Questions.SuccessText: The revision replaces a vague word with specific sensory details about wind and snow.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

Questions.Prompt: Classic TV adaptation: Which actor portrayed Mary Ingalls?
Questions.Hint: Her first name is also Melissa, like the actor who played Laura.
Questions.SuccessText: Melissa Sue Anderson portrayed Mary Ingalls in the classic television adaptation.
Questions.SourceTitle: Peacock: Original Little House Cast and Series

Questions.Prompt: Imagined school supply task: Twenty-four slates are placed equally on 6 shelves. How many slates go on each shelf?
Questions.Hint: Find 24 divided by 6.
Questions.SuccessText: Twenty-four divided into 6 equal groups gives 4 on each shelf. This is an imagined problem.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

Areas.Name: De Smet and Rocky Ridge
Areas.Description: Connect Laura's years in Dakota Territory with her later work, writing, and publication in Missouri through timelines, maps, and media literacy.

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: Which pair of events is connected with Laura's years near De Smet?
Options: Teaching school and marrying Almanzo Wilder
Publishing her first book and moving to Wisconsin
Acting in the 1974 television series and directing episodes
Founding the Osage Nation and mapping Kansas
Questions.Hint: These events happened while Laura was a young woman in Dakota Territory.
Questions.SuccessText: Laura taught near De Smet and married Almanzo Wilder in 1885.
Questions.SourceTitle: The Little House Series — Library of Congress NLS

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: Where did Laura write the Little House books during her later life?
Options: At Rocky Ridge Farm in Missouri
At the Iowa College for the Blind
Questions.Hint: Laura and Almanzo settled near Mansfield.
Questions.SuccessText: Laura wrote the books while living at Rocky Ridge Farm near Mansfield, Missouri.
Questions.SourceTitle: New Facilities for the Cather and Wilder Sites — National Park Service

Questions.Prompt: Actual-life timeline: Laura was born in 1867 and Little House in the Big Woods was published in 1932. How old did she turn that year?
Questions.Hint: Subtract 1867 from 1932.
Questions.SuccessText: 1932 − 1867 = 65. Laura became a successful book author later in life.
Questions.SourceTitle: Wilder, Laura Ingalls — Minnesota Historical Society

Questions.Prompt: Actual life: Who encouraged Laura's writing and provided editorial help as her memories developed into books?
Questions.Hint: She was also a professional writer.
Questions.SuccessText: Rose Wilder Lane encouraged and assisted her mother. Scholars continue to study how their editorial work shaped the books.
Questions.SourceTitle: Today in History: February 7 — Library of Congress

Questions.Prompt: Imagined town budget: A learner has 40 cents. Paper costs 18 cents and a pencil costs 7 cents. How much remains after both purchases?
Questions.Hint: Add the costs, then subtract from 40.
Questions.SuccessText: The items cost 25 cents, and 40 − 25 leaves 15 cents. These are invented prices for math practice.
Questions.SourceTitle: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

Questions.Prompt: Imagined route map: One centimeter represents 50 miles. Two towns are 3 centimeters apart on the map. What distance does the map represent?
Questions.Hint: Multiply the map length by the miles per centimeter.
Questions.SuccessText: Three groups of 50 miles equal 150 miles. This map is an imagined learning tool, not Laura's exact route map.
Questions.SourceTitle: C3 Framework for Social Studies

Questions.Prompt: Classic TV adaptation: Who portrayed Nellie Oleson?
Questions.Hint: PBS's documentary interviews this actor about playing Nellie.
Questions.SuccessText: Alison Arngrim portrayed Nellie Oleson in the classic television adaptation.
Questions.SourceTitle: Laura Ingalls Wilder: Prairie to Page — PBS American Masters

Questions.Prompt: Research skills: Which source note gives a reader the best chance to verify a claim about Laura's life?
Options: A named museum or archive page with a direct link
Questions.Hint: Verification requires enough information to find and evaluate the source.
Questions.SuccessText: A named, linked source lets readers inspect its evidence, author, institution, and purpose.
Questions.SourceTitle: C3 Framework for Social Studies
